body: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer warned the European Union on Monday that a record-breaking loan to Airbus from the European Investment Bank threatens a delicate transatlantic trade truce, including a deal on financing large civil aircraft (LCA) projects. In a statement, Greer expressed frustration that despite "ongoing requests," his office has received no details about the $3.4 billion loan made in June from the EIB, the EU's official lending arm. Boeing had asked the US government in July to press for transparency on the loan, which came amid speculation that Airbus would use the funds to develop a new aircraft model.

"This situation injects substantial uncertainty into transatlantic trade in the aerospace sector," Greer said. "It is important this situation is resolved as soon as possible to ensure market-driven production in the aerospace sector and to avoid violation of the terms of our hard-won LCA deal." The US and EU fought a protracted 17-year battle over alleged aircraft subsidies at the World Trade Organization before agreeing to a five-year truce in 2021 that forestalled mutual tariffs on some $11.5 billion worth of trade, and the truce was extended in July after the EU parliament approved a broader US trade deal. A key question for USTR is whether the terms of the EIB loan would be considered a subsidy for Airbus, as the WTO has found in the past on such loans, while the EIB said in July that it finances thousands of companies every year and denied offering Airbus any unusual support.
en.summary: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer warned the EU that a record-breaking $3.4 billion European Investment Bank loan to Airbus made in June threatens a delicate transatlantic trade truce, including a deal on financing large civil aircraft projects, after his office received no details despite ongoing requests.
en.title: USTR Greer warns EU that Airbus loan threatens trade truce on aircraft financing

facts.claim: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer warned the European Union that a record-breaking loan to Airbus from the European Investment Bank threatens a delicate transatlantic trade truce, including a deal on financing large civil aircraft projects.
Greer expressed frustration that despite ongoing requests, his office has received no details about the $3.4 billion loan made in June from the EIB, the EU's official lending arm.
Boeing had asked the US government in July to press for transparency on the loan, which came amid speculation that Airbus would use the funds to develop a new aircraft model.

The US and EU fought a protracted 17-year battle over alleged aircraft subsidies at the World Trade Organization before agreeing to a five-year truce in 2021 that forestalled mutual tariffs on some $11.5 billion worth of trade, and the truce was extended in July after the EU parliament approved a broader US trade deal.
A key question for USTR is whether the terms of the EIB loan would be considered a subsidy for Airbus, as the WTO has found in the past on such loans.

The EIB said in July that it finances thousands of companies every year and denied offering Airbus any unusual support, describing the loan as a normal loan carrying interest, and Airbus Chief Financial Officer Thomas Toepfer told reporters in London in July that the loan had been taken out completely at market level.

body: 美國貿易代表格里爾週一警告歐盟，歐洲投資銀行6月向空中巴士提供的破紀錄34億美元貸款，恐威脅脆弱的跨大西洋貿易休戰，包括大型民用飛機融資協議。格里爾表示，儘管美方持續提出要求，貿易代表署至今未收到有關這筆貸款的細節；波音7月已要求美國政府施壓要求透明，外界揣測空中巴士可能用這筆資金開發新機型。

美歐曾就飛機補貼在世界貿易組織纏訟17年，2021年達成5年休戰，暫緩對115億美元貿易互徵關稅；休戰已於7月延長，歐洲議會批准更廣泛的美歐貿易協議，以取消美國工業品關稅換取美國對多數歐盟商品課徵15%關稅。美國貿易代表署關注的關鍵問題是，歐洲投資銀行貸款條件是否會被視為對空中巴士的補貼；歐洲投資銀行7月表示每年融資數千家企業，並否認給予空中巴士異常支持，空中巴士財務長7月在倫敦表示這筆貸款完全按市場條件取得。
zh.summary: 美國貿易代表格里爾警告歐盟，歐洲投資銀行6月向空中巴士提供的34億美元貸款恐威脅跨大西洋貿易休戰與大型民用飛機融資協議；美方至今未獲貸款細節，波音7月已要求美方政府施壓要求透明。
zh.title: 美貿易代表警告歐盟：歐洲投資銀行向空中巴士貸款恐衝擊貿易休戰
